gaps.title: How the winning supplier is chosen is not covered
gaps.description: REQ-001 requires awarding a package to one supplier. DEC-001 answered who may award but not how the supplier is chosen. The Award Package form on PKG-104 contains only an Award note field and the button; no supplier selection is shown in the capture. Each package already displays a single Supplier value while Open, so it is unclear whether the award goes to that pre-set supplier or to one chosen from quotes or another list.
gaps.why_it_matters: The award is final (DEC-002), so the supplier it is made to must be unambiguous; the supplier selected also determines who receives the win email (REQ-003, DEC-004).
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: The award action cannot be specified; a package could be awarded to the wrong supplier with no way to correct it.

gaps.title: Award action outcome, confirmation and failure states unobserved
gaps.description: The Award Package button on PKG-104 has no target in the capture. Whether a confirmation step precedes the award, and what is shown on success, on failure, or while the award is processing, is not shown in the capture. DEC-002 states the award cannot be withdrawn, changed or undone by anyone.
gaps.why_it_matters: Because an award is irreversible for everyone, a single accidental click on Award Package permanently locks the package and emails the supplier.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Accidental or mistaken awards cannot be prevented or recovered, and users cannot tell whether an award succeeded or failed.
research_questions: What confirmation patterns do established design systems (for example GOV.UK Design System or Atlassian Design System) recommend for irreversible actions?
How should success and failure of an irreversible submission be communicated to users, including to assistive technology?

gaps.title: Simultaneous or repeated award of the same package
gaps.description: Any Procurement team member can award any package (DEC-001) and the award is final (DEC-002). What happens when two members award the same package at once, when the button is pressed twice, or when a member awards from a stale page after someone else already awarded it, is not stated and not shown in the capture.

evidence_refs.locator: ambiguous_behaviours SCR-012, awarded more than once question

gaps.why_it_matters: REQ-001 limits an award to one supplier and the award cannot be undone, so a double or concurrent award would create a permanent contradiction and could email more than one supplier or the same supplier twice.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: A package could end up with two conflicting final awards or duplicate win emails, with no permitted correction.
research_questions: What established techniques prevent double submission and concurrent conflicting updates for a one-time state transition in web applications (for example idempotency keys, optimistic concurrency)?

gaps.title: Award Package availability for users outside the Procurement team
gaps.description: DEC-001 restricts awarding to the Procurement team. The capture shows only an enabled button on an Open package and a disabled button on an Awarded package; what users outside Procurement see (hidden, disabled, or enabled), which conditions disable the button, and whether a reason is shown are not shown in the capture. Which users can see which packages is also not stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: Only Procurement may make an irreversible award, so the restriction must be expressed for every other user who can reach a package page.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Non-Procurement users may be offered, or able to trigger, an action they are not allowed to take, or may see packages they should not.

gaps.title: Win email recipient address and delivery failure
gaps.description: DEC-004 says only the winning supplier is emailed when the award is made, naming the package and award date. Which supplier email address or contact receives it, where that address comes from, and what happens if sending fails or bounces are not stated. No supplier contact data appears in the capture.
gaps.why_it_matters: REQ-003 is a must and the award cannot be undone, so a failed or misdirected email cannot be compensated by re-doing the award.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: A supplier may never learn it won, and Procurement may not know the email failed.
research_questions: What are common practices for detecting and handling transactional email bounces and send failures (for example provider webhooks, retry policies)?

gaps.title: Whether a package can be awarded without quotes
gaps.description: PKG-104 shows "No quotes attached yet." while the Award Package button is enabled. Whether at least one quote is required before awarding, and how quotes relate to the awarded supplier, is not stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: An irreversible award made with no quote on file may be unintended, and the precondition affects when the button is enabled.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Award eligibility rules cannot be specified; packages may be awarded prematurely.

gaps.title: Award note rules and visibility after award
gaps.description: The Award note textarea has no visible required marker. Whether it is required, any length limit, how validation errors are shown, and whether the note is stored and shown on the awarded package are not stated; the awarded PKG-105 page in the capture shows no note.
gaps.why_it_matters: Because all fields lock after award (DEC-003), the note can only be entered once and cannot be corrected later.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Notes may be lost, missing, or uneditable mistakes, and validation behaviour cannot be specified.

gaps.title: Traceability of who awarded a package
gaps.description: The awarded package shows only an award date; the awarding user is not shown in the capture. Whether the award must record who made it, when, and with which note, and who can view that record, is not stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: Any Procurement member can make a final, uncorrectable award, so accountability for disputed awards depends on what is recorded.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Disputed or mistaken awards cannot be traced to a person or time.

gaps.title: Accessible communication of disabled award and award result
gaps.description: On the awarded package the Award Package button is disabled with no explanation shown in the capture. How the disabled state and the award result are conveyed to keyboard and screen-reader users is not stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: The read-only state of awarded packages and the result of an irreversible award are the key states users need to perceive in this feature.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Some users may not understand why they cannot act or whether the award happened.
research_questions: What does WCAG 2.2 AA (for example SC 4.1.3 Status Messages) require for announcing the result of a form submission?
What guidance exists on disabled buttons versus explained unavailable actions for accessibility?

gaps.title: Package list empty, no-result and scale behaviour
gaps.description: The Supplier packages table shows two rows. Behaviour with no packages, search with no results, which fields search matches, sorting, filtering and paging, and the full set of status values are not shown in the capture.
gaps.why_it_matters: The list is the only entry point to packages awaiting award; Procurement needs to find Open packages among Awarded ones.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: List and search behaviour cannot be specified beyond the two-row default.

gaps.title: Award date format and time zone
gaps.description: The awarded package shows "Awarded on 2 Oct 2026" and the win email must name the award date (DEC-004). The date format, time zone used to determine the date, and whether the email and screen use the same representation are not stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: The award date is communicated externally to suppliers and cannot be corrected after award.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Suppliers and Procurement may see different award dates around midnight or across time zones.
research_questions: What are recommended practices for storing and displaying event dates across time zones in user-facing emails and screens?

gaps.title: Reports page scope
gaps.description: The Reports page shows only "Coming soon." and is reachable from every screen. Whether reports are part of this feature, what they contain and who can view them is not stated.
gaps.why_it_matters: A navigable placeholder in the mockup may imply scope that the requirements do not mention.
gaps.consequences_if_unresolved: Scope of the feature may be misread during specification.

assumptions.text: The product can identify which signed-in users belong to the Procurement team.
assumptions.why: DEC-001 restricts awarding to the Procurement team but nothing in the inputs shows how team membership is known.
assumptions.impact: Permission gaps (GAP-004) assume membership is determinable; if not, an additional identity or role gap exists.
assumptions.to_confirm: How Procurement team membership is held and checked.

assumptions.text: DEC-003 (all fields locked for everyone) is treated as answering CQ-003 even though the decision records no actions.
assumptions.why: The verbatim answer addresses the read-only question directly.
assumptions.impact: No gap is raised about read-only scope.
assumptions.to_confirm: That DEC-003 is the accepted answer for REQ-002 scope.

proposed_status_changes.reason: How the winning supplier is chosen is not stated by DEC-001 and no supplier selection is shown in the capture (GAP-001).
